still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and the oral Wegovy starting dose still costs $149 a month there.
Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone, the GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of that kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 44.0% ever-used − 33.5% current = 10.5% of adults used and are off now. About 54% of current users are on a second or later course (18.1 points), and 3.0 points cycled and are off again, so (18.1 + 3.0) / 44.0 ≈ 48% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.5 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with the parent's persistence figures (about one-third at one year on cash weekly/oral products, ~60% in clinic and conditioned tracks) and restart rates of 36–47%. Persistence rose slightly because track enrolment grew and oral amycretin got a $299 TrumpRx price. Age check: 0.20×21 + 0.33×34 + 0.24×46 + 0.23×30.5 = 4.2 + 11.22 + 11.04 + 7.02 ≈ 33.5. Income thirds average 33.5. Users: 33.5% of ~276M adults ≈ 92.5M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~22.0M (of which ~15.5M are in conditioned tracks); Medicare ~17.0M (~2M of them disabled under-65 beneficiaries; the other ~2.9M users aged 65+ pay cash); Medicaid ~6.5M (~1.6M on AUD labels, ~0.6M children, the rest in the 7 adult-weight states and on CV/diabetes codes); legitimate cash ~37.5M (including ~3.6M calm/focus subscribers, ~7.5M on the $149 starting dose indefinitely and ~9M on TrumpRx oral amycretin); gray market ~9.5M (up from 5.8M). Sum: 22.0 + 17.0 + 6.5 + 37.5 + 9.5 = 92.5. On-label AUD users ≈ 4.9M (Medicare 1.3, Medicaid 1.6, commercial 0.7, cash 1.3). The bottom third rose 17.5 → 26.5. Roughly 4 of those 9 points came through the regrown gray market, 3 through cheaper TrumpRx tiers and 2 through Medicaid AUD coverage. Adult obesity ~30.8%. About 17% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: about 1.16M of ~73M under-18s, flat at 1.6%. 12–17s rose to ~4.3% (~1.08M) while 6–11s fell from 0.45% to ~0.35% (~84k) after the 2035 safety communication and the eleven state under-12 laws. About 31k children in restricting states had their prescriptions lapse at continuation because they could not reach a pediatric endocrinologist. About 7M children now live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~17.0M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk and AUD codes, behind prior authorisation, and pays nothing for weight alone. The tirzepatide dementia label extended to adults 60+ without CVD in Oct 2035. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 17.0M × ~$215 average net/month × 12 ≈ $43.9B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up (up from ~$38.3B). Dementia route: ~3.4M × $230 × 12 ≈ $9.4B. AUD route: ~1.3M × $195 × 12 ≈ $3.0B. The CY2036 Part D guidance lets plans apply 'continuation-of-therapy criteria' using pharmacy adherence data, and about 40% of MA-PD plans now require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered to renew a PA. Medicaid (~6.5M): AUD remains a covered outpatient use in every state. 7 states still cover adult weight loss, and 5 states (up from 2) now condition that coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Children reach semaglutide under EPSDT, but in 11 states initiation under 12 now legally requires a pediatric endocrinologist.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Indian firms launched generic oral semaglutide tablets domestically in 2035. Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses through licensed channels, the product still costs ~$90–180 under the Section 232 tariff. Transshipped API relabelled through third countries and domestic US peptide synthesis now undercut that. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 40–75 and BRL 150–260. India and China supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 37% of employers cover weight-management use, but ~78% of those require verified adherence and/or ≥5% loss at six months. Unconditional coverage is ~8% of employers. Conditioned tracks hold ~15.5M enrollees inside ~22.0M commercial users. Managed decline in prices: the TrumpRx Wegovy pill starting dose is $149 and maintenance dropped to $179. Oral amycretin entered TrumpRx in Mar 2035 at $299 (from ~$449 direct). Foundayo is $149–199, injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $229–279, MariTide $229 direct, retatrutide $349 cash. Brand prices step down without any channel going below $149. Orals are ~68% of users. Gray market regrew to ~9.5M: ~3.5M on 503A-style 'personalised' compounded oral semaglutide and amycretin troches sold through telehealth ($99–179), ~2.5M on 'research use only' retatrutide vials from domestic peptide synthesisers ($120–220), ~1.5M on Mexican border-pharmacy and mail product ($60–140), and ~2.0M on re-filled vials and counterfeit pens. Retatrutide RUO is the fastest-growing segment because it delivers the class's best efficacy at below the price of the branded $299 pill.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill, Jan 2033; orforglipron / Foundayo, Feb 2036). VA/DoD guideline (Apr 2036) lists incretins alongside naltrexone as first-line pharmacotherapy
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide). Strengthened Warnings and Precautions on growth and puberty since Jun 2035, with a medication guide and no REMS

reduction of risk of all-cause dementia (tirzepatide): adults with obesity and established CVD, extended Oct 2035 to adults 60+ with obesity without CVD, with a hip-fracture warning and baseline DXA for women 70+
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and, in California and New York, renamed 'craving care' low-dose plans via telehealth (~3.6M subscribers), ~35% written on AUD labels
sub-threshold 'drink less' use, now also on Foundayo
dementia-prevention use by 50–59-year-olds below the label age, cash-paid
gray-market 'research' retatrutide for weight loss at uncontrolled doses
adolescent use above label titration in gray channels, and 6–11 use in restricting states via out-of-state telehealth
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral-parity driver is realised with an existing product. No new oral above ~21.5% was approved. Oral amycretin's TrumpRx listing in Mar 2035 at $299 made parity mass-market, and orals are now ~68% of users. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. Orforglipron AUD was filed Jan 2035 and approved Feb 2036 (13 months). Tirzepatide's dementia 60+ resubmission went in Mar 2035 as a class 2 resubmission and was approved Oct 2035 with fracture language. Implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. Novo filed a higher-dose oral amycretin (Dec 2035) and it is under review, with no approval before 2037. The first two gastroparesis bellwethers (2035) split: one defense verdict and one $41M plaintiff verdict in New Jersey. Global incretin market ~$215B (2035). US branded net prices fell ~5–7% a year through negotiated channels, faster than in the previous step.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside tracks. Compounded troches with unlabelled strength produce titration-skipping GI emergencies.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Persistence after stopping is still disputed. Claims passed ~47,000. The first bellwethers split one each way in 2035.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling; MDL settlement talks rumoured, none announced.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Higher in gray-market retatrutide users who lose weight fastest.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Pleaded together with EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; folded into the EPI mass tort.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The fracture excess in women 70+ on tirzepatide is now on the dementia label. Lean-mass loss is highest in unmonitored gray retatrutide users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA required at baseline for women 70+ on the dementia indication; bimagrumab ~260k users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No adult signal, including AUD-label users. The pediatric psychiatric signal is about restrictive eating, not suicidality.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia at maintenance doses vs ~3.5% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. The low-dose rate is still unmeasured. An FDA-funded PCORnet study of calm-plan doses enrolled in 2036 and will read out in 2038.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. California and New York laws restrict mood claims in incretin marketing. FDA sent untitled letters and took no enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. New regain cohorts: children whose prescriptions lapsed in restricting states, and track members dropped for adherence gaps.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage and Part D continuation criteria.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine deficiency (in AUD users who keep drinking). Low ferritin in adolescent girls is now linked to the pubertal-delay signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language; thiamine counselling on both AUD labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims ~61,000. The DOJ civil investigative demand remains open.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled on semaglutide and tirzepatide; Novo under FDA follow-up inspection (2035), no warning letter.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. There are no data on indefinite starting-dose use or on long-term gray retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue and were expanded in 2035 to require puberty staging through age 18.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~44,000. RUO retatrutide is linked to tachyarrhythmia ED visits and 10× dosing errors from unlabelled concentration. Re-filled vial infection clusters recurred in Alabama and Texas (2035, ~140 cases, 2 deaths). Poison-centre calls are ~6× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to 70+ telehealth compounders and an import alert on RUO peptides. The Section 232 tariff remains. State pharmacy boards opened cases but enforcement is slow. No federal statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR 48-month update shows a persistent ~0.6 cm/year height-velocity deficit and, in the first near-adult-height subset (n≈310), ~1.4 cm below predicted. A PEDSnet/Medicaid claims analysis of ~88,000 adolescents who started at 12–13 found menarche and Tanner progression delayed ~8–10 months versus matched controls. Swedish registry ARFID HR rose to ~2.2. The signal is concentrated in Medicaid children because they are most of the young starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Jun 2035) and strengthened Warnings and Precautions; no boxed warning and no REMS. 11 states require a pediatric endocrinologist to start a child under 12. AAP reaffirmed lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,000 person-years of ketoacidosis or severe dehydration in titration-phase bingers, confirmed in postmarketing data. Early Foundayo data look similar.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling on both AUD products; ED discharge protocols from ACEP.

safety_ledger.effect: Delayed-puberty-linked psychiatric and social effects in adolescents (low mood, body-image distress, school withdrawal)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The same PEDSnet cohort shows a small excess of depression diagnoses (HR ~1.25) in adolescents with delayed puberty, which may be confounded by obesity stigma. Data on boys are thin.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Included in the 2035 Drug Safety Communication as 'under evaluation'.

food_and_beverage.state: About 48% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are ~16% below 2025 and sugary drinks ~14% below. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed as gray-market users returned. Dollar sales are down ~2% in real terms. Mondelez and PepsiCo close two US snack lines each. Store planning runs by zip and by payer mix.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes ~22% below 2025 and beer ~14%, with the Foundayo AUD label and VA/DoD guidance adding pressure. Kentucky bourbon has cut ~3,100 jobs since 2033. Distributor consolidation continues in Ohio and Indiana. Non-alcoholic drinks pass 6% of category dollars. Brewers push 'session' products to the calm-plan market.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Late-night and bar revenue in Midwestern mid-size cities keeps falling. Casual chains run 'half-plate' pricing. QSR value menus gain in Memphis and the Delta and lose again as the gray market regrows. Protein bowls are the growth format in upper-income suburbs.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists shrink further. Mass retailers stock a two-way run (size-down from gray retatrutide users, size-up from track drop-outs). Structured athletic wear and tailoring carry the upper tier.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. InBody scans are contract requirements in 15.5M track memberships. Budget gyms expand in the South, and 'family strength' programmes spread in upper-income suburbs, helped by the pediatric safety communication.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 37% and mostly conditioned. Pharmacy trend ~+6%. Part D premiums rose for 2036, and continuation criteria arrived in MA-PD. Adherence feeds are now standard vendor infrastructure. Five Medicaid programmes condition coverage.

pharma.state: Global market ~$215B. Volume growth outruns falling net prices. Novo rides oral amycretin despite litigation and an open DOJ inquiry. Lilly gained the dementia 60+ and Foundayo AUD labels. Domestic peptide CDMOs and RUO sellers form an unregulated parallel industry in Texas, Florida and Arizona.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape now reads as a payer-and-income map with sharper lines. Lifted, scanned and slowly lean means a track or a $299 TrumpRx amycretin plan with a gym. Soft and slow-thin means the $149 starting pill. Fast, gaunt and muscle-poor, the look Houston and Phoenix call 'peptide thin', means research retatrutide bought from a website. Regaining means you missed a log, lost a job, or your child's clinic closed the file.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness alone no longer signals money. In Charlotte and Austin, muscle plus visible leanness 'without the gaunt' is the uniform, and refusing drugs for your children is a status act. In lower-income Houston, the Rio Grande Valley and Memphis, the gray market made people thinner than the insured but not stronger. Clinicians at Ben Taub see sarcopenia in 40-year-olds. Pediatric use splits the same way: Medicaid children carry the growth signal, and their parents in Mississippi and Tennessee now face laws telling them to drive to Jackson or Memphis for an endocrinologist.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter. Dayton and Toledo pill nights have spread to Louisville and Indianapolis. Bread Alone claims ~1,400 congregations. School fights moved from recording medication to whether school nurses must report suspected restrictive eating in medicated children.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps list 'on AUD treatment', 'calm plan' and now 'off-drug' as tags. Among Austin professionals, 'off-drug' is the status tag. Couples split over whether a child should start.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Upper-tier appetite is a managed variable. In the Delta, appetite stopped being 'the hunger tax' and became a supply problem again, solved by a website. The MAHA side won its laws, and the restriction politics split it: red-state under-12 laws versus blue-state ad bans on 'calm'. Both claim to protect children and adults from pharma.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia is ~7% vs 3.5% in controls (~10% on retatrutide); the low-dose rate is unmeasured, with a PCORnet study underway. Calm/focus subscribers grew 2.4M → 3.6M. About 35% are written on the AUD labels, now including Foundayo, so platforms can advertise 'craving-free' on-label. California and New York now bar mood claims, and there the same products sell as 'craving care'. Gray RUO retatrutide users, the highest-dose and unmonitored group, report blunting in forums at rates nobody has measured.
interior_life.framing: Platforms sell a feature ('quiet the noise', 'quiet the bottle', 'craving care'). Manufacturers say 'food noise' and 'heavy drinking days'. HR says steadiness. Clinicians say dose-related blunting. Unmuted says sedation. State legislators in Sacramento and Albany call it 'unapproved mood marketing'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 15.5M employees live in conditioned tracks, and an adherence gap can move a family's premium tier. EAPs at trucking, warehousing and call-centre firms offer Foundayo for AUD at no copay. FMCSA still says nothing on calm plans. Benefit brokers still buy de-identified focus cohorts. The two EEOC charges remain open, and a third was filed by an Amazon fulfilment worker who lost a track tier during a pill-bottle sync outage.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir and dry stand-up are mainstream. Columbus and Louisville have lost more live-music nights. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling. A Nashville songwriting scene markets 'unmedicated' sessions as a selling point.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Pill windows and shot days structure mornings. Couples therapists see sober-on-pill versus drinking-partner splits, and now parents divided over a child's prescription after the 2035 safety communication.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The first state restrictions passed: 11 under-12 prescribing laws, mostly in the South and Mountain West, and mood-marketing bans in California, New York and New Jersey. None touched adult conditioning or the gray market. Gray-market users have no lobby. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence, though 2036 campaign ads targeted 'calm' voters as a demographic.

state.regulatory_posture: The federal government is permissive on approvals (Foundayo AUD, tirzepatide dementia 60+) and on manufacturer pricing. It warned on pediatric use without restricting it, and enforces against the gray market by warning letter and import alert with little effect. States moved for the first time, in opposite directions on different targets.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy. The CY2036 Part D guidance lets plans use adherence-based continuation criteria. OPM's FEHB conditions continue. Five Medicaid programmes condition coverage. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands, and Illinois is still the only state banning adherence-conditioned premiums.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Smart-bottle logs are bundled with oral amycretin and now Foundayo starter kits. PBM adherence data flow to MA-PD plans for continuation decisions. Wellness vendors hold track data on 15.5M people. The state under-12 laws require prescriber registration of pediatric starts in 4 states.
state.workforce_or_military: VA/DoD lists incretins as first-line AUD pharmacotherapy. TRICARE covers both AUD labels. The Army recruit oral pilot continues unexpanded. FMCSA guidance is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 100% tariff and India's export checks remain. A WTO panel was constituted on China's complaint, with no ruling. Chinese API transshipped through Vietnam and the UAE with relabelled origin, plus small domestic peptide synthesisers, feed the regrown gray market. Indian generic oral semaglutide launched abroad. Branded US and Danish plants are exempt.

events.event: TrumpRx lists Novo's oral amycretin at $299 a month and cuts the Wegovy pill maintenance price to $179; within a year about 9 million people buy the tablet that matches tirzepatide's weight loss for cash, and orals reach two-thirds of users

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication after a Medicaid claims study of 88,000 adolescents finds puberty delayed eight to ten months in those started at 12–13 and the first near-adult height data show a 1.4 cm deficit in children started at 6–11; labels are strengthened, with no boxed warning

FDA warning letters to more than 70 telehealth compounders and an import alert on 'research use only' peptides fail to halt a regrown gray market of about 9.5 million users, a quarter of them on unapproved-source retatrutide made by domestic peptide labs

CMS's 2036 Part D guidance lets plans renew incretin prior authorisations only for patients whose pharmacy data show 80% adherence; employer coverage reaches 37%, almost four-fifths of it conditional, and track enrolment hits 15.5 million

FDA approves Lilly's orforglipron pill for alcohol use disorder, the second incretin addiction label; in April the VA and Defense Department list incretins as first-line drinking treatment, and employee assistance programmes add it at no copay

Mississippi becomes the eleventh state to require a pediatric endocrinologist to start incretins in children under 12, while California and New York laws barring 'calm' and mood claims in prescription-drug marketing take effect; Medicaid families sue, arguing the state laws defeat federal EPSDT coverage

open_tensions: Eleven states now gate under-12 prescribing behind pediatric endocrinologists that rural Medicaid families cannot reach. About 31,000 children stopped and are regaining, and an EPSDT lawsuit asks whether a state practice law can override a federal coverage mandate. Meanwhile adolescents started at 12–13 are going through delayed puberty, and nobody knows their adult heights.

The poorest users now take the class's strongest molecule, retatrutide, as unregulated 'research' vials at higher doses than the insured, with no monitoring. The tariff that was meant to end the gray market made it domestic.

Conditioning has reached Medicare through continuation criteria and covers 15.5M workers through tracks. An adherence log decides coverage for tens of millions of people, and Illinois is still the only state that limits it.

The calm-plan, AUD-label and EAP channels have merged into one blunting market of 3.6M subscribers plus 4.9M on-label AUD users. State ad bans changed the vocabulary, not the product, and the low-dose anhedonia data will not arrive until 2038.

prose.headline: One in Three: The Pill Got Cheaper, the Insured Got Logged, and the Poor Got Thin on Peptides Nobody Approved
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, roughly ninety-two million people. Most of them swallow it. The tablet that matched the injections, Novo's oral amycretin, went onto the TrumpRx cash menu in March 2035 at $299 a month. Within a year about nine million people were buying it there, and two of every three users now take a pill. Prices fell the way the administration wanted them to, through deals and in steps. The Wegovy starting pill is still $149, the maintenance dose dropped to $179, and no branded product sells below that floor. The list price of Wegovy is still $1,349 and is paid by no one.

Coverage expanded and tightened in the same motion. More employers cover the drugs than ever, about thirty-seven percent, but four in five of them pay only for members whose pill bottles report on time and whose scans show progress. Fifteen and a half million workers live inside those tracks. In December 2035 the logic reached Medicare. Plans may now renew a prescription only if pharmacy data show the patient took it. Medicare still pays nothing for weight loss as such. It pays for hearts, kidneys, sleep apnea, drinking and, since October 2035, dementia risk in anyone over sixty with obesity, which together cover most of the people it would have covered anyway.

The drinking label doubled. Lilly's Foundayo pill was approved for alcohol use disorder in February 2036. The VA and the Pentagon now list incretins as first-line treatment, and warehouse and trucking employers hand the pill out through assistance programmes with no copay. Kentucky's bourbon towns have lost more than three thousand jobs since 2033. The calm platforms grew to three and a half million subscribers, a third of them written on an alcohol diagnosis. In California and New York a new law bars them from promising calm, so there they sell 'craving care'.

The children's story turned. In June 2035 the FDA reported what the claims data showed. Adolescents who started at twelve or thirteen reach puberty eight to ten months late, and the first children started at six to eleven to approach adult height are about a centimetre and a half short. There was no boxed warning, only stronger language. Upper-income parents had already opted out. The children carrying the signal are mostly on Medicaid, because Medicaid children were most of the young starters. Eleven states, Mississippi the latest, now require a pediatric endocrinologist to start a child under twelve. In the Delta that means a drive to Jackson, and thirty thousand prescriptions lapsed at renewal. Families are suing, arguing that federal children's coverage rules override the state laws.

The tariff of 2033 did not end the gray market. It moved it home. Chinese powder now arrives relabelled from Vietnam, and small peptide labs in Texas and Florida sell retatrutide marked 'not for human use' for about $180 a vial. That is less than the branded pill and stronger than anything a pharmacist can dispense. Telehealth compounders sell semaglutide troches of uncertain strength. Warning letters went to seventy of them, and nine and a half million people buy outside the law anyway. In Houston clinicians have a name for what they see, peptide thin: forty-year-olds who are lighter than the insured and weaker than their parents.

So the body now reads as a payer. Lean and lifted means a track and a gym. Soft and slowly thinner means the $149 pill. Gaunt means a website. Regaining means a missed log, a lost job or a closed clinic file. The country eats sixteen percent fewer snacks and drinks a fifth less whiskey than it did in 2025. From a distance it looks calmer. Up close the calm is billed, logged and, for the poorest, cut in a back room.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tanya Bell wakes at 5:10 in Southaven and takes the vial out of the butter compartment. The label says RESEARCH USE ONLY in a font made to look like Pfizer's. She draws to the line her cousin marked on the syringe with a Sharpie, a little under, because last month her heart raced through a whole shift.

She has lost forty-one pounds since March. At Kroger her old neighbour said she looked sick, then asked for the website.

She drives to her first client, Mr. Odom, eighty-three. His Zepbound comes in a box from his Part D plan with a card about bone scans. She counts his pills into the organiser. He tells her she's wasting away. She says thank you.

At noon she eats half a turkey sandwich in the car and calls the clinic in Jackson about Dre. He's ten. He took the Medicaid shots for fourteen months and grew, the nurse said, a little slow. The state wants a specialist now. The first opening is in February. The woman on the phone is kind about it.

She calls her sister in Memphis, who is on the $149 pill and has been for two years. 'It doesn't do much,' her sister says. 'But it does something.'

After school Dre eats two bowls of cereal and asks why he can't have his medicine. She says the law changed. He asks if it's because he did something.

At night she orders the next vial, $184 with shipping, from a Houston address. The confirmation email says Thank you for supporting independent science. She deletes it and sets the alarm.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly 4 of those 9 points came through the regrown gray market, 3 through cheaper TrumpRx tiers and 2 through Medicaid AUD coverage.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the bottom third is about 92M adults, so 2 points is about 1.8M people. That exceeds the world's own total of ~1.6M Medicaid AUD users, and Medicaid AUD only grew by about 0.7M since 2034.
